newsitem.title: UK: Russia Eurobond to boost engineering area - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Russia Eurobond to boost engineering area - Merrill.

text.p: Russia's $1.0 billion Eurobond debut on Thursday and plans for further borrowing through 1997 will boost spending on electrical utilities, which means increased orders for the country's engineering sector, Merrill Lynch analyst Maxim Shashenkov said in a note to investors.

"We believe that electric utility equipment suppliers stand to benefit from the fact that for the first time in six years, there are potential buyers with real hard cash for their products," Merrill said.

The bank believes that Russia could raise as much as $2.0 billion next year and funds will be used to rehabilitate the electricity sector which, unlike the telecommunications sector, is supplied almost exclusively by domestic companies.
There will also be a pickup from the oil sector once production-sharing agreements in the Caspian region are signed.
Although the engineering sector is currently in poor shape, slow changes, such as growing exports and competitiveness, will provide a boost.
Merrill identifies Uralmash, Izhorsky Zavod, Leningradsky Metal Plant and Kirovsky Zavod as leading companies in the market. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
